dish: Show-stopping custom specialty cakes, scones and from-scratch cookies
w: Barb Talevich's bakery-café on West Market at Overwood (with a second shop in Green), baking everything on site for ~30 years. Signal Akron readers placed it 2nd for Best Bakery in the 2026 Best of the City vote and profiled it ('making memories sweeter for nearly 30 years'); Akron Life has featured its decorators and cakes.

dish: Prime steaks with Lanning's famed sauce off the open grill; martinis poured tableside
w: Bath Township's special-occasion steakhouse over Yellow Creek (opened 1970); bought in 2020, renovated (~$2M) and relaunched as Dean Martin's Lanning's with tuxedoed service and a dress code. Cleveland Magazine: 'a classic Akron restaurant reimagined'; Akron Life feature on the transformation; Wine Spectator Award of Excellence (2022).

dish: Rack of lamb and seafood brought in fresh daily
w: Moe Schneider's from-scratch restaurant (1998) in a former Front Street supermarket — a fine-dining room plus a tavern side. On Cleveland Magazine's 'Cuyahoga Falls' 18 Best Restaurants and Bars' (fresh seafood, lamb, unique appetizers) and written up by Akron Life ('There's Moe to Come').

dish: Chori pollo fajitas — chicken smothered in chorizo and cheese, served sizzling
w: Family Mexican kitchen with an open patio on Portage Trail. On Cleveland Magazine's Cuyahoga Falls best-restaurants guide (which singles out the chori pollo fajitas) and voted 2nd Best Mexican Restaurant in Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards.

dish: Sparta's steaks and chops alongside Greek and Italian plates
w: Family-run Canton steakhouse with 60+ years behind it, now cooking weekly-changing Greek, Italian and international specials around the traditional steaks. Voted 2nd Best Steakhouse in Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards; listed by Visit Canton.

dish: Cut-to-order cheese flights with wine pairings, and cheese-centric sandwiches
w: Downtown Canton's artisan cheese house — world cheeses cut to order, dine-in flights, a deli counter and grazing boards. One of the Canton Repository's picks in 'Eat your way through downtown Canton'; listed by Visit Canton.

dish: Tiger Musky Double IPA, Creek Chub Mango Gose and Yellow Perch Cream Ale
w: Arts District microbrewery (2018) whose beers are named for freshwater fish and local lakes (Sippo Lake Vienna lager). Akron Life profile ('Fishing for beer'); on the Canton Repository's downtown dining-and-drinks guide; listed by Visit Canton.

dish: Skillets, omelets and pancakes beside the tracks
w: Kent's breakfast institution, now in the 1875 Atlantic & Great Western depot above the Cuyahoga (two-hour Sunday waits). Kent Stater Best of Kent 2026 — first place, Best Breakfast; Ohio Magazine Best Hometowns (Kent); News 5 and The Portager covered the move into the depot.

dish: House helles and seasonal beers, plus Moscow mules and slushies
w: Mill District brewery (opened Nov 2020) beside the historic Star of the West mill. Kent Stater Best of Kent 2025 Best Brewery; Ohio Magazine Best Hometowns (Kent) names it in the Mill District; The Portager's Portage County breweries round-up.

dish: Nitro cold brew and beans roasted on site
w: Mark and Michelle Kemp's Stark County roaster (2016); the Erie Street shop is the largest of the small chain and where the beans are roasted. In the Canton Repository's 'Caffeinate your way through Stark County with these 6 coffee roasters'; listed by Visit Canton.

dish: Smoked meats and from-scratch sandwiches and burgers — with 1,000+ board games to play
w: Board-game tavern in a former Wadsworth bowling alley. The Akron Beacon Journal's Local Flavor review ('great fun in Wadsworth') praised the depth of flavor; the Medina Gazette covered its opening.

Downtown Barberton's craft brewery and taproom (ribbon-cut 2018; a second taproom later opened in Brunswick). In Ohio Magazine's Ohio Craft Beer Guide; WKYC 'First Look' marked its five-year anniversary in Barberton.
